title: The surah opens by shaking the ground under you.
subtitle: A call to all people before the Hour

row.title: mindfulness of the Lord
sub: the event is the reason, He is the focus

then: These opening lines came in late Makkah, shortly before the migration. Ibn Kathir records the Prophet ﷺ reciting them aloud on a journey so the Companions hurried to catch up. When they grew sad, he told them: {reward}be of good cheer and strive hard.{/reward}
now: You feel a small earthquake one night. The lamp sways, the phone buzzes with alerts, and for ten seconds everything you were worried about vanishes. {idea}That clarity is what this verse wants to keep alive{/idea}, without waiting for the ground to move.
old: The end of the world is a scary topic I would rather not think about.
new: The verse names the shaking so I will turn toward my Lord now, while I still can.
try: Next time you feel a jolt of fear today, use it as a reminder to say one sincere prayer.

title: A day so heavy a mother forgets her baby.
subtitle: The strongest bonds go quiet on that Day
then: The verse picks the tightest bond a person knows, a mother and the child at her breast. On that Day {trap}even that bond is forgotten{/trap}. The listeners in Makkah understood: nothing they relied on would hold their attention then.
now: Think of the person you would run into a burning house for. Now picture a moment so heavy even that love goes silent. {idea}The verse is not cruel. It is honest about how big the Day is{/idea}, so you prepare while love and time are still in your hands.
old: My family and my love for them will carry me through anything.
new: Love is a gift for here; on that Day each soul stands with its own deeds.
try: Do one kind act for someone you love today, and intend it for Allah.

title: Arguing about Allah with nothing but noise.
subtitle: Debate without knowledge, and who you end up following
then: Ibn Kathir says this describes people who denied the Resurrection and argued about Allah {trap}without sound knowledge{/trap}. One report names An-Nadr bin Al-Harith, a Makkan who argued against the message. Their arguing felt like independence, but they were following whoever pushed them.
now: A clip in your feed mocks faith in thirty seconds. The comments pile on. You feel a pull to argue back, or to agree, before you have read a single page. {idea}Strong opinions with no study are an open door{/idea} for whoever speaks loudest.
old: I have heard enough to have a firm opinion on this.
new: An opinion without knowledge is just an invitation for someone else to steer me.
try: Before sharing a view on a faith question today, look up one reliable source first.

title: Befriend the devil and he guides you, the wrong way.
subtitle: What is written about following Shaytan
then: Ibn Kathir explains that it is written for Shaytan: {trap}whoever follows and imitates him, he misleads{/trap}, and drives toward the Fire. The verse uses the word guide on purpose. Shaytan also leads; the question is where.
now: The friend who always knows the shortcut, the late-night app that always has one more video, the voice that says you deserve it this once. Each one leads somewhere. {idea}Ask where the path ends, not how easy the first step is.{/idea}
old: I am not following anyone; I am just doing what feels right.
new: Everyone follows someone; I should check where my guide is taking me.
try: Pick one habit you slid into without deciding. Ask honestly where it leads.

title: Doubt the raising again? Look at how you began.
subtitle: Your own life story and the rain on dead earth

row.title: child to strength
sub: then old age, or earlier death

row.title: barren earth
sub: rain falls, it stirs and blooms

then: Addressed to people in doubt about the Resurrection. Ibn Kathir notes that when Allah mentions this denial, He answers with {idea}evidence from how He starts creation{/idea}: the stages in the womb, the arc from weakness to strength to weakness, and the dry ground that swells after rain.
now: You hold an ultrasound printout, a grey blur that will soon have a name. Or you visit a grandparent who no longer remembers your face. Or you see a brown lawn turn green after one storm. {reward}Every one of those is the verse, playing out in front of you.{/reward}
old: Life after death is hard to believe; it is beyond anything I have seen.
new: I have seen life come from nothing many times; the second time is not harder.
try: Look at a photo of yourself as a baby today and think about who brought you this far.

title: Behind every blooming field: He is the Truth.
subtitle: Why the signs of the last verse happen

row.title: He gives life to the dead
a message
sub: He gives life, and will again

then: The verse explains the signs just described. Ibn Kathir says Allah is {idea}the Creator and Controller who does as He wills{/idea}, and just as He gives life to the dead earth He gives life to the dead. Listeners who doubted were pointed at their own fields.
now: You scroll past a time-lapse of a seed splitting and a shoot pushing up. Two seconds, then the next video. {idea}The verse asks you to stop the scroll{/idea} and read the caption it gives: He is the Truth.
old: Nature runs by itself; there is nothing more to see.
new: Every return of life is a small signed note from the One who will raise me.
try: Water a plant or step outside today and say quietly: He gives life to the dead.

title: The Hour is coming, and the graves will open.
subtitle: Two certainties the signs point to
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}it will inevitably come to pass{/idea}, and Allah will bring people back after they have become dust. This closes the argument that began with the stages of creation and the rain on dry soil.
now: You stand at a fresh grave after a funeral. Everyone is quiet, someone's phone vibrates, cars wait outside. It feels final. {reward}The verse says it is not the end of the story{/reward}, only a pause before everyone stands again.
old: When people die, they are simply gone.
new: The grave is a waiting room; the One who made us will raise us.
try: Make a short prayer today for someone you have lost, by name.

title: No knowledge, no guidance, no book, still loud.
subtitle: The one who leads the arguing

row.title: verse 8
sub: the one who leads others astray

then: Ibn Kathir notes the shift: verse 3 described blind followers, {trap}this verse describes their leaders{/trap}, who call others to error with no rational proof and no transmitted text, only opinion and desire.
now: You are in the family group chat and you post a confident take on religion you half remember from a video. Three cousins forward it. {idea}Now you are not just wrong, you are leading.{/idea} The verse asks what you are standing on before you speak.
old: If I sound sure, people will see I know what I am talking about.
new: Confidence is not knowledge; I am responsible for where my words lead others.
try: Next time you want to state a religious claim, add the source or stay quiet.

title: Turning his neck away, and dragging others with him.
subtitle: Arrogance that refuses the truth when called
then: Ibn Abbas said the phrase means {trap}too proud to follow the truth when called to it{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to Luqman telling his son not to turn his cheek from people in pride. The posture is the problem, not a lack of evidence.
now: Someone younger than you points out a mistake at work, politely, in a meeting. You feel your jaw tighten and your head turn to the screen. {idea}That small turn is the gesture this verse describes.{/idea}
old: I would accept the truth if someone gave me good reasons.
new: Sometimes the reasons are there and only my pride is turning away.
try: Today, when corrected, face the person, say thank you, and think about it before replying.

title: This is what your own hands sent ahead.
subtitle: Allah wrongs no one
then: Ibn Kathir says these words are spoken {trap}as a rebuke{/trap} to the arrogant arguer of the previous verses. He meets only what his hands sent forth, and Allah is not unjust to His servants.
now: Every message you send, every hour you spend, every kindness or cruelty goes ahead of you like a parcel in the post. {reward}The good news hides inside the warning: the good ones arrive too.{/reward}
old: What happens to me in the end is out of my hands.
new: My hands are sending things ahead every day, and nothing is lost or added unfairly.
try: Send one good thing ahead today: a call, a gift, a forgiveness.

title: Worshipping on the edge, ready to leave if it hurts.
subtitle: Faith that only stays while life goes well

row.title: a bond
sub: it holds in good and hard

then: Ibn Abbas described people who came to Madinah and said {trap}this is a good religion{/trap} if a son and a foal were born, and a bad one if not. When illness or delay came, Shaytan whispered that faith had brought only trouble.
now: You started praying regularly, then you got the job. Then the job ended, and the prayer mat stayed rolled up in the corner. {idea}The verse is not shaming you. It is naming the edge{/idea} so you can step back from it toward solid ground.
old: If I do my part and things still go wrong, maybe faith is not working.
new: Faith is not a payment for good days; it is what keeps me standing on bad ones.
try: Pray one prayer today in a hard moment, not a good one, and tell Allah how you feel.

title: He calls on what can neither help nor hurt.
subtitle: Where the edge-worshipper turns next
then: Continuing the picture of verse 11. Ibn Kathir says the person turns to {trap}idols and rivals{/trap} for help, support and provision, which can neither benefit nor harm him. Leaving Allah in a trial does not lead somewhere better.
now: After a bad month you start checking your horoscope, or pinning your hopes on a lucky charm, or a get-rich scheme a friend swears by. {idea}None of it can lift a finger.{/idea} The verse calls that a long way off course.
old: When God does not seem to answer, I should try something else.
new: What I run to instead has no power at all; the door I left is the only real one.
try: Notice one thing you lean on for luck. Replace it today with a short dua.

title: A friend whose harm arrives before any help.
subtitle: How wretched a protector, how wretched a companion

row.title: harmful
sub: it costs you more than it gives

then: Ibn Kathir says this one is {trap}more likely to harm than benefit{/trap} in this world, and certainly harms in the next. The word for companion means the one you mix with and spend your time with.
now: The thing you open every time you feel low: the betting app, the bottle, the friend who only drags you down. It promises comfort and delivers the hangover first. {idea}The verse asks: is this a protector, or a bad companion?{/idea}
old: This habit or this friend comforts me when nothing else does.
new: If the harm shows up before the help, it was never my protector.
try: Spend ten minutes today with a companion who leaves you better, not worse.

title: Belief plus good deeds, and gardens with rivers.
subtitle: The other path after all the warnings
then: After the doomed comes the blessed. Ibn Kathir describes people who {idea}believe firmly in their hearts and confirm it with action{/idea}, doing good and avoiding evil. The verse ends: Allah does what He wills.
now: After a long day of bad news, someone sends you a photo of a quiet river. You exhale. {reward}This verse is that exhale{/reward}, after many verses of warning. The door to the gardens is belief that shows up in what you do.
old: After so many warnings, I wonder if there is any hope for me.
new: The path is clear and open: believe, and let it show in what I do.
try: Do one good deed today that matches something you believe.
